# SizedRegion

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:sized-region` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A region that gives content which cannot size itself a definite height: fill the room its parent gives, a typed height, or minimum and maximum bounds.

## When to use

Give a whole-screen layout (TabNavigator, NavStack, SplitView, Workbench) placed below an app's root a usable height. Those layouts fill their parent's height and have none of their own, so in a parent that sizes to its content they collapse to their bar.

- A whole-screen layout sits below the app's root, beside other content in a Pane's content, or in a region the app sizes, and should fill the room it is given.
- A whole-screen layout must keep a usable height in a parent that sizes to its content; give the region a minHeight or a length.
- Bound a whole-screen layout's height with maxHeight so it does not grow past a readable size.

**Not when:**

- Do not wrap a whole-screen layout that is already the app's root or fills a Pane the app sizes; it fills that height on its own.
- Do not use SizedRegion to force an ordinary component's size; components size to their content and tokens, and List, Grid, Row, and SunkenPanel have their own fill and flex props.
- Do not rely on min-height in app CSS around a whole-screen layout; it does not give the layout a definite height. Use SizedRegion's minHeight.

**Alternatives:**

- [List](./list.md) (parent-sizing-alternative) — Use List's fill, flex, minHeight, and maxHeight to size a List itself.
- [ResizableRegion](./resize.md) (nearest) — Use ResizableRegion when the person drags to change the size.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/sized-region` — exports `SizedRegion`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/sized-region` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/sized-region.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/sized-region`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuisized-region) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- fill (default)
- typed height
- minimum and maximum bounds

**CSS-value props** (typed builders from `@kerfjs/ui/css-values`; raw CSS strings are rejected):

- `height`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `fill`; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `height="fill"`
- `minHeight`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `minHeight={rem(20)}`
- `maxHeight`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `maxHeight={rem(40)}`

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the height, or the parent height a fill takes; the bounds; the content.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- A one-cell grid: its child fills the region, and a minHeight alone gives that child a definite height. fill grows within a flex column (a Pane's content) or takes all of a parent with a definite height; in a parent that sizes to its content it has nothing to take.

## Accessibility

- SizedRegion is a plain structural div with no role; its content keeps its own landmarks and names.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-sized-region`.

Never put `kui-sized-region` on an element you write; render `SizedRegion` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
